title: Project 1b: a second card
content:
Now make a different card that shares the first one's DNA. Maybe it's the channel card that sits next to videos, or a playlist card. Same corners, same spacing, same type, different content and shape. Doing this by copy and paste shows you why the next chapter, design systems, exists.

  • Read and watch: about 10 minutes
  • Do: about 1 hour
  • You make: two related cards side by side in one pen
  • You need: your Project 1 pen
  • Support level: medium: fewer steps, same tools

Read

  • CSS custom properties (MDN): variables in CSS.
  • A guide to flexbox (CSS-Tricks): how to sit cards next to each other.

Do

Keep the original untouched. Fork it and work in the copy.

Move the values both cards share (radius, gap, border, font) into CSS variables at the top. Give each card a shared class plus its own:

Model it on paper first, like last time. Then build it with the shared class and only the CSS that makes it different.

Wrap both in .wrapper with display: flex. Add a third card. On a phone they should stack.

Change --card-radius to 0. Both cards change at once. That's the point.

Stuck? Ask your study buddy

Use AI to explain, not to do the work for you. Paste your own code or error with the prompt, read the answer, then close the chat and type the fix yourself. If you can't explain the fix out loud, you don't own it yet.

You're done when

Journal it

Add a heading for this page to your dev journal (the public Gist you made in Start here) and answer in Markdown:

  • Link the forked pen.
  • What did both cards share? What made them different?
  • How did copying CSS between them feel? What would happen with 40 cards?
